schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digits (n TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, segment VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, region VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, created_day SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, account_id INT NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, created_day SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, amount_cents INT NOT NULL) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS order_items (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, order_id INT NOT NULL, sku_id INT NOT NULL, qty TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL, unit_price_cents INT NOT NULL) ENGINE=InnoDB
generation_sql: INSERT IGNORE INTO accounts (id, segment, region, created_day) SELECT seq.n, CASE WHEN seq.n <= 500 THEN 'premium' ELSE 'standard' END, ELT(1 + MOD(seq.n, 4), 'na', 'eu', 'apac', 'latam'), 1 + MOD(seq.n, 365) FROM (SELECT (d1.n + 10*d2.n + 100*d3.n + 1000*d4.n + 10000*d5.n) + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 CROSS JOIN digits d4 CROSS JOIN digits d5) AS seq WHERE seq.n <= {row_count}

INSERT IGNORE INTO orders (id, account_id, status, created_day, amount_cents) SELECT seq.n, CASE WHEN MOD(seq.n, 2) = 0 THEN 1 + MOD(seq.n, 500) ELSE 501 + MOD(seq.n, 49500) END, CASE WHEN MOD(seq.n, 20) < 17 THEN 'paid' WHEN MOD(seq.n, 20) < 19 THEN 'shipped' ELSE 'cancelled' END, 1 + MOD(seq.n, 365), 500 + MOD(seq.n, 50000) FROM (SELECT (d1.n + 10*d2.n + 100*d3.n + 1000*d4.n + 10000*d5.n + 100000*d6.n) + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 CROSS JOIN digits d4 CROSS JOIN digits d5 CROSS JOIN digits d6) AS seq WHERE seq.n <= {row_count} * 3

INSERT IGNORE INTO order_items (id, order_id, sku_id, qty, unit_price_cents) SELECT seq.n, 1 + FLOOR((seq.n - 1) / 3), 1 + MOD(seq.n, 10000), 1 + MOD(seq.n, 5), 100 + MOD(seq.n, 900) FROM (SELECT (d1.n + 10*d2.n + 100*d3.n + 1000*d4.n + 10000*d5.n + 100000*d6.n) + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 CROSS JOIN digits d4 CROSS JOIN digits d5 CROSS JOIN digits d6) AS seq WHERE seq.n <= {row_count} * 9
ANALYZE TABLE digits, accounts, orders, order_items

tables.name: digits
tables.purpose: helper number source for bounded synthetic row generation
tables.distribution_notes: Fixed 0-9 seed table used only to generate larger row sets deterministically.

tables.name: accounts
tables.purpose: parent entity with a rare premium segment filter and evenly spread regions
tables.distribution_notes: Premium rows are sparse; region is roughly uniform across four values; primary key only, no secondary index on segment or region.

tables.name: orders
tables.purpose: high-volume child table joined from accounts
tables.distribution_notes: Half of the rows repeatedly point to the first 500 premium accounts; status is heavily skewed toward paid/shipped; no index on account_id or status.

tables.name: order_items
tables.distribution_notes: Exactly three items per order on average; no index on order_id, so join fanout remains expensive under concurrency.

value_skew.orders.account_id: about half the orders target the first 500 premium accounts to create repeated lookups
value_skew.accounts.region: approximately uniform across na, eu, apac, latam

join_selectivity.orders.account_id = accounts.id: many-to-one with high repetition on a small hot subset

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE a.region, COUNT(*) AS item_count, SUM(oi.qty * oi.unit_price_cents) AS gross_cents FROM accounts a JOIN orders o ON o.account_id = a.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE a.segment = 'premium' AND o.status IN ('paid','shipped') GROUP BY a.region ORDER BY gross_cents DESC
calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the synthetic schema preserves the intended join fanout and forces the optimizer to consider a broad join path over the large child tables.
expected_evidence: The plan shows the join order and broad row estimates for the orders and order_items tables.
The join predicates are visible without a supporting secondary index on account_id or order_id.
The plan reflects fanout-heavy scanning rather than a narrow point lookup.
